DOJ’s later OPR statement describes the resolution of the 2006–2008 federal investigation.
Exact investigation endpoints, non-prosecution-agreement dates and state-plea dates are not established by this selected statement.
The July 8 SDNY announcement reports that Epstein was arrested on the preceding Saturday.
The source’s relative wording is retained; no exact arrest date is added.
SDNY announced two federal charges against Epstein and the unsealing of an indictment.
Charges are allegations, not a conviction; the underlying indictment was not acquired for this selection.
The June 27, 2023 OIG announcement records Epstein’s death on August 10, 2019 while in Bureau of Prisons custody.
This uses a retrospective official statement. Detailed circumstances are excluded.
DOJ announced release of the executive summary of OPR’s investigation into the earlier federal case’s resolution.
The full OPR report and underlying agreement were not acquired.
DOJ reported that OPR found poor judgment by former U.S. Attorney Acosta and shortcomings in victim treatment, while finding no professional misconduct by Department attorneys.
This dates the public description, not when investigators reached the findings. An oversight finding is not a criminal conviction.
SDNY reported that a unanimous jury found Ghislaine Maxwell guilty.
This is the prosecutor’s announcement; the verdict form was not separately acquired.
Date and first sentence of the statement
SDNY reported a 240-month prison sentence and five years of supervised release imposed on Maxwell.
An imposed sentence does not establish time served or current custody. No monetary penalty is normalized or described as paid.
Opening paragraph and closing sentencing paragraph

OIG announced its BOP custody and supervision report, described serious staff failures and eight recommendations accepted by BOP, and reported no evidence contradicting the separate FBI conclusion concerning criminality connected to the death.
The announcement is the selected source. Agreement with recommendations is not implementation; the full report was not acquired.
PDF page 1 opening; page 2 findings and recommendations
DOJ announced a first phase of declassified files, describing many records as previously leaked before formal government publication.
This does not establish the first publication date of every underlying document. No released files were opened.
The House Committee’s September 2 announcement says its chair issued a records subpoena to DOJ on August 5.
The year follows the dated announcement’s context. The subpoena itself was not acquired.
The House Committee announced release of 33,295 pages provided by DOJ.
This is an announced page count, not an independently counted file total. The transfer date is unknown and overlap with DOJ releases is unresolved.
The House Committee announced an additional 20,000 pages of documents received from Epstein’s estate.
Receipt date and file count are unknown. Official publication does not verify every enclosed statement.
The official text records Public Law 119-38, approved November 19, 2025. Section 2(a) specifies publication of covered material within 30 days.
First publication or disclosure of the enacted text is unknown here. No statutory-compliance conclusion is made.
